source.dataset: GEOS-FP 2 km replay (model), 19 August 2025 20:00 UTC. Sound design adapted from team BoboMimi's TerraJuke

legend.summary: Four kinds of particles in the air, from NASA's GEOS model at one moment, 19 August 2025: smoke, dust, sea salt and sulfate. Each has its own instrument, and all four play together as Earth turns under the needle, west to east.
legend.method: The instrument tells you which particle: smoky brass is smoke from fires, desert strings are dust, a soft ocean bed is sea salt, glass bells are sulfate from pollution and volcanoes. Higher notes mean the particles sit further north, and sound more in your left ear; further south is lower, and more in your right. Louder means thicker. Clear air is silent.

items.meaning: Black carbon (smoke). Louder where there is more of it.
Dust. Louder where there is more of it.
Sea salt. Louder where there is more of it.
Sulfate. Louder where there is more of it.

legend.caveat: GEOS is a model analysis, not a direct measurement, and NASA's colour bar has no numbers, so loudness follows how strongly a place shows each colour, not how many particles are there. One moment, not a live feed.

frames.label: Around the world
frames.caption: NASA's GEOS model of the air on 19 August 2025 at 20:00 UTC. Earth turns under the needle, west to east.
frames.alt: NASA GEOS model map of aerosols on 19 August 2025: green sulfate streams across both hemispheres, a lilac river of Saharan dust over the Atlantic, orange-red fire smoke over southern Africa and Spain, and pale blue sea-salt swirls over the oceans, including Hurricane Erin.

frames.label: The Saharan dust journey
frames.place: Sahara to the Atlantic and the Caribbean
frames.caption: Desert dust from the Sahara crosses the whole Atlantic, hazing Caribbean skies and reaching the United States.
frames.alt: The Saharan dust journey: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around Sahara to the Atlantic and the Caribbean.

frames.label: Hurricane Erin
frames.caption: The first Atlantic hurricane of 2025. Its winds churn the ocean, lifting sea salt into blue spirals, while it draws in dust from Africa.
frames.alt: Hurricane Erin: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around the western Atlantic.

frames.label: Southern African fire smoke
frames.caption: Seasonal farm burning sends smoke drifting out over the Atlantic Ocean.
frames.alt: Southern African fire smoke: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around southern Africa and the Atlantic.

frames.label: Wildfires in Spain
frames.caption: Wildfires raging across several regions of Spain add smoke to the European sky.
frames.alt: Wildfires in Spain: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around the Iberian Peninsula.

frames.label: Mount Etna's plume
frames.caption: Italy's Mount Etna releases streams of sulfate particles over southern Europe.
frames.alt: Mount Etna's plume: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around Sicily and southern Europe.

frames.label: Kilauea's sulfate stream
frames.caption: Hawaii's Kilauea volcano sends a narrow stream of sulfate particles westward across the Pacific.
frames.alt: Kilauea's sulfate stream: the NASA aerosol map, with a box around Hawaii and the central Pacific.
